extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers and policy/regulatory analysts in finance studying IPO communication, market microstructure, and disclosure effects
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical study design and evaluation of how IPO quiet-period regulations affect firm communications (press releases, earnings announcements), stock-return synchronicity, trading volume, and analyst coverage. Includes sample construction, measurement choices, hypotheses, regression specifications, and compliance proxies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample selection and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with all U.S. IPOs with an issue date from January 1996 through December 2011; exclude unit offerings, ADRs, spin-offs, reverse LBOs, closed-end funds, REITs, any IPO of non-common shares, and firms already filing with the SEC at the time of IPO (typically >500 shareholders or publicly traded bonds). Final sample: 3,380 IPOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start sample in 1996 to ensure uniform disclosure regime after PSLRA, availability of EDGAR filings (Form S-1), and adequate I/B/E/S coverage. Use SDC Platinum (augmented with Jay Ritter), CRSP, Compustat, I/B/E/S, Factiva. Be explicit about exclusion rules and document final sample size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press-release measurement window and collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Hand collect news articles in the 20 days before and after quiet period expiration (21-day window centered on day 0) using Factiva's Intelligent Indexing; count firm-initiated press releases and categorize press-release-wire items as firm-generated communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For firms not in Intelligent Indexing, perform free-text company name searches and manually scan results to confirm relevance. Use raw counts for descriptives and log transformations (ΔLog press release) in multivariate regressions to capture relative changes. Also separately count press releases occurring during the quiet period for 'quiet period loudness' measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matched control firm selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Match each IPO firm to an existing public control firm using the closest market capitalization on the IPO firm's quiet-period-expiration day; measure control-firm synchronicity over the exact same windows as the matched IPO firm and compute relative synchronicity as IPO synchronicity minus control synchronicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the control firm's measures are computed over identical calendar windows to the IPO firm to facilitate difference-in-differences (or relative) comparisons; report that results are robust to this matching choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stock-return synchronicity measurement and transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Report raw R^2 (synchronicity) values in descriptive statistics/univariate analyses, but use a log-odds transformation of R^2 in all multivariate regression analyses (equation [2]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about reporting raw R^2 for interpretability but transform for regression analysis to address skew and interpretability; note robustness checks using adjusted R^2 and winsorization of non-positive adjusted R^2 values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volatility measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure mean daily volatility as the standard deviation of daily returns over the same windows used for synchronicity; note that overall volatility remains relatively stable from during to after the quiet period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because option-implied volatility is often unavailable immediately after IPO, use realized daily-return standard deviation. Include the change in volatility as a control in synchronicity regressions to ensure synchronicity effects are not driven by volatility changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trading-volume reaction measurement for earnings announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute volume changes as the difference in total volume between trading-day window [−4,−2] and trading-day window [−1,+1], with day 0 as the earnings announcement date; analyze relative declines using logs to account for general aftermarket decline in volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate cases where the [−4,−2] window includes the offer date to avoid distortion. Expect smaller declines in volume for earnings releases after the quiet period and for quiet-period releases accompanied by press releases or conference calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regression specification for press-release activity (Equation [3])
rubrics_metrics.description: Regress the relative change in press release activity (ΔLog press release) on Log analyst coverage, High RD (indicator), Log MVE, Underpricing, and controls including Log S-1 amendments, ΔVolume, Offer price, Underwriter rank (Carter-Manaster), Registration time, Age at IPO, B/M, H-index, and Retained interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypothesis #1 predicts negative coefficients for β1 (Log analyst coverage), β3 (Underpricing) and β4 (?), and a positive coefficient for β2 (High RD). Report both univariate and multivariate results (use logs in regressions to capture percentage changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regression specification for change in synchronicity (Equation [4])
rubrics_metrics.description: Regress change in synchronicity on Log MVE, Log analyst coverage, High RD, Underpricing, ΔLog press release, interactive terms (e.g., Log MVE × ΔLog press release, High RD × ΔLog press release, Underpricing × ΔLog press release, Log analyst coverage × ΔLog press release), and controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypothesis #2: ΔLog press release (β5) should be negative (greater releases → larger synchronicity drop). Interaction predictions: β6, β8, and β9 positive, and β7 negative (as stated in the paper) — interpret interactions carefully and present marginal effects. Use within-firm and relative-to-control measures as robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis-testing framework and use of univariate + multivariate analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Form explicit hypotheses (#1, #2, #3) about which firms increase communication and how communication affects synchronicity/volume; first present univariate patterns and figures, then test in multivariate regressions with controls and interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine graphical and tabular univariate evidence with multivariate regressions. Explicitly state expected coefficient signs for hypothesis testing and discuss consistency between univariate and multivariate results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quiet-period regime classification (25-day vs 40-day)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify firms into pre-Global-Settlement (25-day quiet period) if IPO date before July 9, 2002, and post-Global-Settlement (40-day quiet period) if IPO date on/after July 9, 2002; compare changes in synchronicity and volatility across regimes using diff-in-diff approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present within-sample and control comparisons; report that changes in synchronicity/volatility between regimes may be insignificantly different and that observed differences could stem from trends in control firms rather than IPO firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earnings-announcement method classification for compliance analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Manually investigate SEC filings, investor-relations pages, and Factiva to classify inaugural earnings releases that occur during the quiet period as: (a) filed via post-effective S-1 amendment / 10-K/10-Q with no press release, (b) accompanied by a press release, and (c) accompanied by a press release plus a conference call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document examples (Appendices B and C) illustrating compliant releases (explicitly stating no conference call) versus apparent violations (quantitative guidance and conference calls). Use these classifications to analyze volume reactions and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators for quiet-period events used in volume regressions (Equation [5])
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Quiet period earnings_i = indicator that earnings announcement fell in the quiet period; Press release_i = indicator that a quiet-period earnings announcement had an accompanying press release; Conference call_i = indicator that the firm held a conference call during the quiet-period earnings announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regress ΔEarnings volume on these indicators plus controls. Expect earnings releases after the quiet period to experience less decline in volume; within quiet-period releases, anticipate press releases and conference calls to be associated with even smaller declines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proxies for quiet-period 'loudness' and 'serious violation'
rubrics_metrics.description: Quiet period loudness_i = log of the number of firm-initiated press releases during the quiet period (count post-IPO but prior to quiet-period expiration). Serious violation_i = indicator equal to 1 if firm gave earnings guidance prior to quiet-period expiration or had an earnings announcement during the quiet period and held a conference call with analysts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For firms with 40-day regimes, results are robust if counting only the first 25 days. Use these proxies as explanatory variables in regressions assessing analyst coverage and forecast outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyst-coverage and forecast-benefit outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure three benefits potentially arising from quiet-period loudness: (1) Log # EPS forecasts_i = number of analysts providing EPS forecasts for the first quarterly earnings release after quiet period (logged), (2) Non-EPS forecast_i = indicator for at least one disaggregated (non-earnings) analyst forecast, (3) Q# meet-beat_i = indicator that firm met or beat mean analyst consensus EPS forecast in initial quarters (up to four).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use I/B/E/S Guidance, CIG First Call, and Capital IQ Company Events for management forecast and analyst-coverage data. Regress these outcomes on Quiet period loudness_i and Serious violation_i (Equation [6]) with controls; expect positive coefficients if 'louder' firms attract more analyst attention and short-term forecasting benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual validation for news-item relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: For firms not captured by Factiva Intelligent Indexing, perform free-text searches and scan individual articles to ensure they relate to the firm in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the manual search procedure and its prevalence; report that the vast majority of firms were included in Intelligent Indexing and note how missing-index cases were handled to ensure comprehensive press-release counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness and reporting conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Report raw descriptive statistics (means, medians) and univariate correlations; in regressions use transformed dependent variables (e.g., logs, log-odds for R^2) and include relevant controls and interaction terms. Check robustness to alternative R^2 measures (adjusted R^2) and winsorization of non-positive values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about which measures are used where (descriptives vs regressions). Provide robustness checks (adjusted R^2, winsorization) and alternative sample splits (e.g., balanced subsamples, regime splits) to support conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of press-release content as firm-generated
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize any articles coming from press release wires as firm-generated communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This classification is used to distinguish management-initiated communications from third-party media coverage. Be transparent about how wire-service items are treated and whether any post-hoc reclassification occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of interaction terms to assess heterogeneity
rubrics_metrics.description: Include interactions between ΔLog press release and firm characteristics (size, R&D intensity, underpricing, analyst coverage) to test whether the effect of increased press releases on synchronicity is stronger for firms that are smaller, high-R&D, more/less underpriced, or have less analyst coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret interaction coefficients in the context of their main effects and report marginal effects for representative values (e.g., below/above-median size). The paper finds stronger press-release effects for smaller and High R&D firms and for firms with less analyst coverage.
